title: Upload embed timeout, Plan 0: local timing of the 30-page fixture (docs/specs/upload-embed-timeout.md)
no_paid_call: local CPU only; no Fly, no production Neo4j, no LLM provider, no model download

environment.machine: Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX (24 logical processors: 8 performance + 16 efficiency cores, no SMT), 63 GB RAM, Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, on AC power (battery 100%, charging state), power scheme 'Turbo', host CPU about 3% before the run
environment.primary_run: Windows native, repo .venv (Python 3.13.13, onnxruntime 1.29.0, numpy 2.5.0, tokenizers 0.22.2), process pinned to performance cores (threads=1: logical cpu 10; threads=2: cpus 10 and 11)
environment.secondary_run: WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 (Python 3.12.3, throwaway venv /tmp/plan0-venv with the deploy/requirements-serve.txt pins: onnxruntime 1.29.0, numpy 2.5.3, tokenizers 0.23.2), vCPUs pinned with sched_setaffinity (threads=1: vcpu 4; threads=2: vcpus 4,5); the host decides which physical core a vCPU runs on
environment.parse_and_chunk: WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04, Python 3.12.3, tokenizers 0.23.2, pypdfium2 5.13.0 (the Linux parse sandbox with RLIMIT_AS); cross-checked on Windows (tokenizers 0.22.2): identical 60 chunks, identical text

model.built_from: models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx (local, sha256 0b2937d85ef4f8fffa223b5fe3418ad481b66eae88099fcb81f96fc70e8cb710) by scripts/predequantize_embedder.py, output to a scratch directory outside the repo (not kept)
model.build_gates: 196/196 nodes bit-exact vs onnxruntime dequantization; cosine gate mean 1.0 / min 1.0 over 53 questions

paths_used.windows_run: <session scratchpad>/fp32model/model_fp32.onnx (+ .onnx.data, tokenizer.json), outside the repo and OneDrive
paths_used.repo_models_dir: untouched; models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-fp32 was absent locally and is still absent

conclusions.spec_reconstruction_13923: not reproduced: the measured embedded total is 228 tokens (1.6%) higher; the 16,000 cap is an upper bound 11.6% above it
conclusions.transfer_to_fly: INFERRED: proportionality is MEASURED on this desktop core (same onnxruntime 1.29.0 and model, different silicon); that a Fly performance core has the same shape is inferred, and so is the 182 to 188 core-s cap-job range below
conclusions.cost_is_proportional_to_tokens: every fit intercept is within 0.05 s of zero (under 5% of a chunk's time; the sweep intercepts are within 2 standard errors of zero, the narrow fixture-only fits extrapolate to a slightly negative -0.015 to -0.043 s); seconds per token is flat to 1% across chunk-size terciles; the 85.8 tok/s figure transfers across chunk shapes (cap job 182 to 188 core-s whatever the chunk count, against 186.5)

reproduce: uv pip install --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 --python-version 3.12 --target <scratch>/linux-site <deploy/requirements-serve.txt pins of numpy onnxruntime tokenizers pypdfium2 pdfplumber pdfminer.six pillow cryptography charset-normalizer rapidfuzz neo4j pydantic pydantic-settings python-dotenv python-docx lxml>
wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04: python3 -m venv --without-pip /tmp/plan0-venv; copy <scratch>/linux-site/. into its site-packages (ensurepip is absent; /tmp is wiped on every WSL restart)
WSL: the same plan0_time.py with --cpus 4 (threads 1) and --cpus 4,5 (threads 2) on /tmp/fp32model/model_fp32.onnx

notes.cap_job_table_s: seconds for the 16,000-token cap job (186.5 performance-core s at 85.8 tok/s) by sustained share and class factor; unchanged from the spec: the table is built on the cap, not on the fixture
notes.fixture_table_s: the same table for the measured fixture, 14,151 tokens at 85.8 tok/s
notes.transfer_to_fly: INFERRED: 85.8 tok/s is a Fly performance-2x figure; the proportionality (zero intercept) was measured on a desktop core with the same onnxruntime and model, not on Fly silicon
notes.boot_shares: whole-job averages (ready_s includes parse, chunking and indexing); the embed-only share is a little higher

boot1_range_vs_rule.note: boot 1's whole-job average is now below the 12% the rule uses over its whole range; 2,100 s clears 1.5x of both by about 5%; the embed-only share is a little higher than a whole-job average
